{{short description|Theorem in topology}}
{{inline-citations|date=February 2020}}In [[geometric topology]], the '''Property P conjecture''' is a statement about [[3-manifold]]s obtained by [[Dehn surgery]] on a [[knot (mathematics)|knot]] in the [[3-sphere]]. A knot in the 3-sphere is said to have '''Property P''' if every 3-manifold obtained by performing (non-trivial) Dehn surgery on the knot is not [[simply-connected]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Celebratio Mathematica — Eliashberg — Filling and topology |url=https://celebratio.org/Eliashberg_Y/article/1197/ |access-date=2025-04-24 |website=celebratio.org |language=en}}</ref> The conjecture states that all knots, except the unknot, have Property P.

Research on Property P was started by [[R. H. Bing]], who popularized the name and conjecture.

This conjecture can be thought of as a first step to resolving the [[Poincaré conjecture]], since the [[Lickorish–Wallace theorem]] says any closed, orientable 3-manifold results from Dehn surgery on a link.<ref>{{Cite thesis |last=Michler |first=Finn |title=The Lickorish-Wallace Theorem |date=June 2024 |degree=Bachelor Thesis |publisher=ETH Zurich |url=https://www.research-collection.ethz.ch/handle/20.500.11850/694486 |doi=10.3929/ethz-b-000694486 |language=en}}</ref>
If a knot <math>K \subset \mathbb{S}^{3}</math> has Property P, then one cannot construct a counterexample to the Poincaré conjecture by surgery along <math>K</math>.

A proof was announced in 2004, as the combined result of efforts of mathematicians working in several different fields.

==Algebraic Formulation==

Let <math>[l], [m] \in \pi_{1}(\mathbb{S}^{3} \setminus K)</math> denote elements corresponding to a preferred longitude and meridian of a tubular neighborhood of <math>K</math>.

<math>K</math> has Property P if and only if its [[Knot group]] is never trivialised by adjoining a relation of the form <math> m = l^{a} </math> for some <math> 0 \ne a \in \mathbb{Z}</math>.
